stem: A Massachusetts provider submitted a program approval request 20 days before the planned presentation date and the Executive Director's designee denied it. The provider wants to challenge the denial. Which statement correctly describes the position?

choices.text: The submission was timely, so the denial can only have been substantive.
The provider may appeal to the full Board by written petition within 30 days of the notice of denial.
The provider must resubmit rather than appeal, because a designee's decision is unreviewable.
The provider may appeal only if it holds current ACPE accreditation.
The provider must appeal within 30 days of the planned presentation date.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 4.04(2) requires a request to be submitted no less than 30 days before the proposed presentation, so a 20-day submission is untimely. 247 CMR 4.04(4) separately allows a provider whose request is denied by the Executive Director or designee to appeal to the full Board by written petition submitted within 30 days of the notice of denial. The two 30-day periods run from different events.

choice_analysis.A: A 20-day submission is untimely against the 30-day advance requirement.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: written petition to the full Board within 30 days of the notice of denial.
choice_analysis.C: A designee's denial is expressly reviewable by the full Board.
choice_analysis.D: ACPE standing bears on authorized-provider status, not on the right to appeal.
choice_analysis.E: The appeal clock runs from the notice of denial, not from the presentation date.

related_facts: A provider in good standing with ACPE or AMA CME Category 1 is considered an authorized provider.
explanation.mpje_trap: Two 30-day clocks appear in the same section and run from different events.

reasoning_steps: Test the submission against the 30-day advance requirement
Separate the advance-submission clock from the appeal clock
Measure the appeal window from the notice of denial
